newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Caltex says revamping Asian management.
newsitem.headline: Caltex says revamping Asian management.

text.p: Caltex Petroleum Corp, a joint venture between U.S. majors Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp, is restructuring of its top management in Asia in order to be more competitive, Chairman David Law-Smith said on Monday.
"We are organising ourselves to be agile and clearly to be in a position to execute strategies within a very prompt time frame," Law-Smith told Reuters in an interview.
He said Caltex, which has it corporate offices in Irving, Texas, would move two corporate vice-presidents to Singapore towards the end of the year.
"The corporate vice-president who is located in Singapore as our Asian connection will in fact speed up the process which would normally come to our corporate office," he said.
The vice-presidents would have corporate responsibility for two areas for the world, basically splitting Caltex operations into two, he said.
Jock D. McKenzie would be vice-president in charge of Southeast Asia and Richard Fernie would be responsible for the Middle East, Africa and South Asia.
Caltex refines and markets petroleum products in 60 countries and territories in the eastern hemisphere.

Law-Smith said the country marketing directors would report to the vice-president in charge of that region. He, in turn, would report to a director and a senior vice president in the corporate office in Texas.
"But it's important to realise that the corporate office really provides the strategy and the resources to execute strategies, capital and people," Law-Smith said.
"It is our executives on the ground and the operating companies that are really accountable for their implementation."

Law-Smith also said Leo Lonnergan would take up the new Singapore position of Chief Operating Executive to coordinate the company's wordwide logistical support, refining, international trading and Singapore terminalling.
"One of our sustainable advantages is that we are decentralised and our operating company executives with their independent boards are responsible for day to day operations," he said.

"The senior position will enhance our capability in the supply and logistic activity of our business, specifically recognising that we are a company short of refining related to our total market requirement and that we have surpluses and deficits in different geographies from our own refineries,' he said.
"In summary, our Singapore presence is being increased dramatically," he said.

Law-Smith said the restructuring was not connected to Monday's launch by Caltex of a $500 million program to support its new brand image as part of plans to improve its marketing position in the world's high growth areas for petroleum.
As part of the programme, the Caltex logo, service stations and convenience stores will be redesigned over the next 30 months, starting in Southeast Asia.
